key_insight: The paper argues that sparse success/failure outcomes from online RL fine-tuning of vision-language-action (VLA) policies should not be compressed into one flat reward signal. Instead, a hierarchical advantage weighting scheme can better turn episode-level outcomes into useful transition-level learning signals.
problem_solved: It addresses the mismatch between sparse binary episode outcomes and the need for per-transition supervision during actor updates in online RL fine-tuning of pretrained VLA policies. A single scalar reward/advantage often mixes different feedback types and becomes less informative once tasks are no longer purely failing.
method: Convert sparse episode outcomes into a structured hierarchy of learning signals rather than one global scalar.
Assign advantage weights at different levels to distinguish distinct transition-level feedback contributions.
Use the hierarchical weighting to provide more informative actor updates during online fine-tuning of VLAs.
impact: For practitioners, this can make online RL fine-tuning more effective when feedback is scarce and only episode success is available. It may improve learning stability and help pretrained VLA agents keep improving beyond simple task completion.
visual_elements: A flow diagram showing pretrained VLA policy -> rollout episode -> binary success/failure -> hierarchical advantage weighting -> actor update
A side-by-side comparison of single-scalar reward vs hierarchical weighting
A layered pyramid or tree icon illustrating outcome-to-transition decomposition
A training curve chart showing improved fine-tuning progress under sparse feedback
paper_title: Hierarchical Advantage Weighting for Online RL Fine-Tuning of VLAs from Sparse Episode Outcomes
paper_authors: Tongyan Fang, Siyuan Huang, Naiyu Fang, Ganlong Zhao, Zhongjin Luo
